C0.quote: We consider voting on multiple independent binary issues.
C0.note: Multi-issue voting, Condorcet winners, issue-wise majority.

C1.quote: it is co-NP-hard to determine whether there exists a Condorcet-winning proposal
C1.note: Complexity and recognition algorithms are most results; Anscombe bounds on distance to IWM are approximation/guarantee results (WD); domain/paradox-free conditions are axiomatic-like (AX). Not SB/EQ.

C2.1.quote: We call the matrix P = (𝑣𝑖,𝑗 )𝑖 ∈ [𝑛],𝑗 ∈ [𝑡 ] the preference profile.

C2.2.quote: Each voter 𝑖 ∈ [𝑛] is modeled as a dimension-𝑡 vector 𝑣𝑖 ∈ B𝑡
C2.2.note: Binary opinion vectors over issues plus weight vectors; voters compare proposals by weighted Hamming distance. Not RANK/APPR in the codebook sense, though induced preference is derived.

C2.3.quote: the opinion/preference 𝑣𝑖,𝑗 ∈ B of voter 𝑖 on issue 𝑗
C2.3.note: Voters have opinions/preferences, and induced preference relations over proposals.

C2.4.quote: the opinion/preference 𝑣𝑖,𝑗 ∈ B of voter 𝑖 on issue 𝑗
C2.4.note: Input described as preference and the rule applied directly; internal weights are 'reported' but no statement on truthfulness.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit held attitude.

C4.1.note: Input is not in the listed ordinal formats; satisfaction only mentioned as future work.

C4.2.note: Term 'dichotomous preferences' used only in citing related work title/reference.

C5.1.note: Evaluation is by agreement with IWM and Condorcet/majority support, not welfare/representation criteria; satisfaction only in future work.

VOT.quote_behav: voter 𝑖 weakly prefers 𝑝 over 𝑝 ′ , written 𝑝 ≽𝑖 𝑝 ′
VOT.note: Voters vote by fixed rule (weighted Hamming distance) in comparisons; no strategic action.

claims.quote: giving a convenient characterization for a whole class of instances
allow for practically certifying “safe instances” where issue-wise majority is the right choice
the chosen proposal should not be easily refuted by calling a vote

C9.1.note: Claims about which rule/proposal to choose (IWM right choice) and real-world implications.

C9.2.quote: where issue-wise majority is the right choice
C9.2.note: Claim that IWM is the 'right choice' needs assumption that submitted opinions equal true preferences and that voters evaluate proposals by weighted agreement; the input-held attitude relation is not stated.
